newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AT LEAST 167 KILLED ON S.AFRICA'S HOLIDAY ROADS.
newsitem.headline: AT LEAST 167 KILLED ON S.AFRICA'S HOLIDAY ROADS.

text.p: At least 167 people have been killed in road accidents in the first week of South Africa's Christmas holiday season, officials said on Tuesday.

Of the overall death toll, 50 were pedestrians while 36 people were killed in head-on collisions. Another 34 died when their cars overturned, the National Traffic Information Centre set up to coordinate the holiday rush said in a statement.

The worst area for fatal road accidents was Gauteng region centred on Johannesburg where 31 people had died from December 3, the official start of the holiday traffic season, followed by 28 in the beach resort haven of the Eastern Cape.

Another 26 people were killed in KwaZulu-Natal centred on the Indian Ocean port of Durban, 25 in Mpumalanga, the game reserve heart of South Africa, and 22 in the Western Cape which has Cape Town as its capital.
In other regions, 14 people were killed in road accidents in Northern Province, 11 in the Free State, nine in the North West, and one in the isolated Northern Cape.

Appealing for increased driver awareness to curb the annual slaughter on the country's roads, traffic centre spokeswoman Christa van der Walt said: "By following safety rules, a large number of deaths can be prevented this holiday period."
Driver fatigue, lack of concentration and unroadworthy vehicles are cited as the main causes of road accidents.
